provenance:
The POINTER half of D8/ADR-034, on the dev proxy the postmortem names for the Citigroup class (§7: 'development iterates on dev proxies -- the cvx-2015/jpm-2024 pointer class'). Chevron FY2015 answers Item 7 in 280 chars and Item 8 in 189 ('The index to Management's Discussion and Analysis, Consolidated Financial Statements and Supplementary Data is presented on page FS-1.'), with 294,291 chars of the real MD&A and financial statements sitting unlabelled in the tail -- ADR-019 §e's internal-pointer-to-a-paginated-section class, enumerated there as permanently-red debt (`evals/adversarial/cvx-2015-internal-pointer.json`). This case does NOT re-litigate that debt: the status stays `extracted` (ADR-004's ruling is untouched and both `item_present` checks assert it), the item text stays served, and the offsets do not move. What changes is that the envelope stops calling it a 0.95 extraction: `item_span_near_empty` carries the item code, so `WARN_PENALTY` takes both items to 0.80 and `review_required` reads true on 7 and 8 and false on the substantive Item 1 (82,907 chars).

It is also the false-positive pin for the document-level half. Chevron puts only 27.18% of its text inside item spans -- the second-lowest coverage of any real dev filing, and the closest to `COVERAGE_MIN = 0.13` after `ge-1994`'s 0.2306 -- so `warning_absent low_item_coverage` here asserts that a legitimately pointer-heavy real filing does NOT escalate to `ambiguous`. RED at `820cf0c`: both `item_span_near_empty` expectations, both confidences (0.95 != 0.8) and all three `review_required` fields (the field did not exist).
